Daily Brief

Monday's global headlines are dominated by dramatic political shifts in South America and the Balkans. In Brazil, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva secured a historic fourth presidential term, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro by more than 4 million votes after a campaign marked by record turnout and deep polarization [France 24, Le Monde, Financial Times]. In Serbia, a student-led protest movement born from the 2024 Novi Sad railway station disaster has ended Aleksandar Vučić's 14-year grip on power, winning over 52% of the vote in snap parliamentary elections that saw the highest turnout in three decades [BBC, RFI, Le Monde]. Meanwhile, regional tensions continue to simmer across the Middle East and Africa: Algeria announced its first foreign troop deployment since 1973 to protect energy infrastructure in Niger [France 24], while Saudi-led coalition forces struck Houthi missile facilities in Yemen following continued attacks on Riyadh's airport [Al Jazeera, The Hindu]. In Paris, European defence ministers from France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK convened to discuss expanded military support for Ukraine amid ongoing Russian strikes [Al Jazeera]. Venezuelan opposition leader María Corina Machado returned home after more than ten months in exile, greeted by crowds of supporters in Caracas [BBC].

Top Stories
01 Geopolitics

Serbia's Student Movement Defeats Vučić in Historic Parliamentary Election

  • A student-led movement called 'Student List-Students Win' won over 52% of the vote in Serbia's snap parliamentary elections, ending 14 years of rule by Aleksandar Vučić's Serbian Progressive Party
  • Vučić conceded defeat less than two hours after polls closed; the election recorded Serbia's highest parliamentary turnout in over 30 years
  • The movement emerged in response to the November 2024 collapse of a canopy at Novi Sad railway station that killed 16 people, widely blamed on government corruption and negligence
  • Celebrations erupted across Belgrade, Novi Sad and other cities as supporters gathered to mark what they called Serbia's 'freedom'

02 Geopolitics

Lula Wins Historic Fourth Term as Brazil's President, Defeating Bolsonaro

  • Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, 80, won Brazil's presidential runoff by approximately 4.4 million votes over Senator Flávio Bolsonaro
  • Turnout was massive, with over 10 million more votes cast for Lula compared to the first round; blank and spoiled ballots reached record lows
  • Bolsonaro has refused to accept the result and announced plans to challenge it, citing a Supreme Court ruling that extended voting hours
  • World leaders including France's Macron and China's government congratulated Lula, while left-wing governments in Latin America celebrated the result

03 Geopolitics

Algeria Approves First Foreign Troop Deployment Since 1973 to Protect Niger Energy Sites

  • Algeria's parliament unanimously approved sending troops to Niger, marking the country's first overseas military deployment since the 1973 Arab-Israeli war
  • The deployment aims to protect energy facilities, including the Trans-Saharan Gas Pipeline project being built jointly by Algeria and Niger
  • Niger faces persistent attacks by armed groups near its border with Algeria; the move follows a thwarted mutiny in Niger in August
  • The two countries share a 960-kilometer desert border and have agreed to deepen cooperation against jihadist violence

04 Conflict

European Defence Ministers Meet in Paris to Discuss Expanded Ukraine Military Support

  • Defence ministers from France, Germany, Italy, Poland and the UK convened in Paris to discuss increasing military assistance to Ukraine
  • The meeting came as Russian strikes injured civilians in Zaporizhzhia and Chernihiv, while Ukrainian drones killed two in Russia's Voronezh region
  • Russia's Defence Ministry claimed strikes on power stations in Kharkiv and Khmelnytskyi regions, as well as port infrastructure in Chornomorsk
  • High-level delegations from Saudi Arabia, Pakistan and Turkey simultaneously met in Tehran seeking to avert renewed Iran-US-Israel conflict

05 Geopolitics

Venezuelan Opposition Leader María Corina Machado Returns After 10 Months in Exile

  • María Corina Machado returned to Venezuela on Sunday after more than 10 months in exile, greeted by supporters in Lara state and later Caracas
  • She had fled Venezuela by speedboat in January to accept the Nobel Peace Prize in Norway
  • Her return follows the US seizure of President Nicolás Maduro and installation of his deputy Delcy Rodríguez as interim president, who subsequently signed an oil deal with Washington
  • Machado was photographed at Mass and travelled to Caracas in a caravan of cheering supporters
